newsitem.title: USA: Miami firm questions Grigsby Brandford disclosure.
newsitem.headline: Miami firm questions Grigsby Brandford disclosure.

text.p: A syndicate member on a $183 million Dade County, Fla., swap deal sent Grigsby Brandford & Co a second letter questioning its disclosure on the deal and suggesting that failure to provide requested information could violate municipal regulations, Reuters learned Wednesday.

The letter from Howard Gary & Co said failure to provide the requested data "could potentially be construed as a willful violation of the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board's Rule G-17, as well as other applicable federal, Florida and local disclosure laws by Grigsby Brandford & Co Inc and its representatives."
The MSRB rule requires municipal securities dealers to "deal fairly with all persons" and specifies that they "shall not engage in any deceptive, dishonest, or unfair practice."

The letter was dated Sept 30 and signed by Kishor Parekh, senior vice president at the Miami firm Howard Gary & Co. It was addressed to Napoleon Brandford III, who resigned as Grigsby Brandford & Co on Tuesday to join another firm.
Officials at Grigsby Brandford were unavailable for comment, and a spokesman at Howard Gary & Co declined to comment, citing company policy.

The letter concerns a Dade County revenue bond issue that closed Sept 10. Grigsby Brandford was senior manager on the deal. Smith Barney Inc was co-senior manager and AIBC Investment Services Corp and Howard Gary & Co were co-managers.

The letter questions why Grigsby Brandford did not disclose in the official statement that the swaps provider, GBR Financial Products, is part owned by Calvin Grigsby and Napolean Brandford, the founders and former owners of Grigsby Brandford and Co.
The letter also asks how much revenue was generated and earned on the swap, and with whom the aggregate capital risk for the swap was placed.

Sources told Reuters that Howard Gary & Co had sent an earlier letter on Sept 10 seeking the same information but got no response. The earlier letter did not raise the issue of compliance with MSRB rules.

Dade County officials declined to comment Wednesday but said previously they knew of the relationship between Grigsby Brandford and GBR Financial Products and were satisfied with disclosure on the deal.
